notes.title: SCP: Observer Anniversary Update
notes.content:
Greetings Survivors,

after a long period of inactivity, a new update I've been working on for the past few months is finally ready. This update aims to be a final overhaul of SCP: Observer, reworking most of the things I was unhappy with.

Some of the changes include a complete overhaul of the menu user interfaces as well as the modding system. Many of these changes are visual and you won't notice much difference in gameplay. Modded skins, however, now include more advanced parameters such as SCP speed or custom sounds.

Cheats and the console have also been improved. Updated cheats can be found in the "Cheats.txt" in the installation folder of SCP: Observer.

If you are interested in modding, you can find the instructions [url=https://github.com/getmyisland/scp-observer-modding]here[/url]. Following the guide is easier than before, but you still need a very basic understanding of the Unity editor.

You can now also play earlier versions of SCP: Observer, e.g. the version before the anniversary update or the first/second beta. To do this right-click on SCP: Observer in your Steam library -> Properties -> Betas -> Beta Participation. WARNING: Playing a different version will also affect your save file and you will not be able to use the Steam Workshop.

Thank you for playing SCP: Observer.

notes.title: Version 1.8.0 - Steam Workshop, Endless Mode and QoL Improvements
notes.content:
Happy spooky month everyone,

SCP: Observer is back with a new update that includes many new additions and improvements. The full list of changes can be found below.

[h2]Steam Workshop[/h2]

First of all, the Steam Workshop. You can now customize skins for featured SCPs and create your own to share with the community. The original plan was to allow the creation of custom maps and custom SCPs, but unfortunately that will not happen in this update.

To download a mod, simply go to the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1738710/workshop/]Steam Workshop for SCP: Observer[/url] and download anything you like. Then launch the game and select the skins you want in the "Mod Manager". Seriously try the new SCP-096 skin, it is terrifying.

To create a custom mod, I recommend you use [url=https://github.com/getmyisland/scp-observer-modding]this GitHub template[/url].

If you have problems, the file: [i]Steam/steamapps/common/SCP_Observer/Mods/INSTRUCTIONS.txt[/i] has a troubleshooting section at the end.

[h2]Endless Mode[/h2]

The endless mode can be activated by selecting Endless instead of Normal in the Custom Scenario screen. The main difference is that, as the name suggests, there is no victory condition and you have to survive as long as you can. The SCPs get stronger over time and the difficulty level increases as well. To compensate for this, the generator now generates more power, so you can regain a lot of lost power. How far can you make it?

[h2]Happy Halloween![/h2]

If you haven't already join my [url=https://discord.gg/Wg8jvxJB4u]Discord server[/url] to keep up with the latest news and updates. Feedback is always welcome, especially on workshop support. Thank you for your support and I wish all of you a scary Halloween.

[h2]Full changelist[/h2]

[list]
[*]Added Steam Workshop support to allow the creation of custom skins
[*]Added Endless mode for Custom Scenarios
[*]Added 5 new achievements
[*]Improved death and win screen
[*]Improved Tutorial by displaying tasks in ui
[*]Improved visiblity of blink and stamina slider
[*]Custom Scenario activity levels can now be entered directly
[*]Security Camera map now shows power and usage
[*]Other minor fixes/improvements
[/list]

notes.title: Version 1.7.0 - Performance and balance improvements
notes.content:
Greetings survivors,

I have some great news to announce. In the past week I have made some performance improvements as well as some balancing changes. As always, you can find the full list of changes below.

Before I start, I want to thank everyone who tried the game after seeing the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YzICf5HFSYY]Markiplier video[/url], and everyone else as well. It really means a lot to me.

First, I made some performance tweaks that improved performance by 30-50 fps for me. These were mostly some boring project configuration settings that are not worth covering.

Secondly, I changed some balancing settings that many people have complained about. The first thing is that SCP-173 is guaranteed to fail on its next 3 movement attempts after looking at him. Before it was 2 and also much more inconsistent. The next thing is that you can now prevent SCP-096 from entering the room by closing the west security door. Believe it or not, that didn't work before (sorry). Lastly, I made the generator a bit more effective, but this change will be the least noticeable of all.

I have also fixed many bugs and apologize to anyone who had issues, especially with the security doors getting stuck. I'm not sure if I fixed the problem as I was never able to replicate the bug, so please let me know if you are still having problems.

[h2]Full changelist[/h2]

[list]
[*]Various performance improvements
[*]Increased SCP-173 move penalty after being watched
[*]Increased generator power generation to a random power between 3-5%
[*]Decreased generator max regenerate time
[*]SCP-096 now moves away when blocked by security door
[*]Added more options for setting the quality
[*]Removed copyrighted SCP-173 images
[*]Separated LC and HC Official Scenarios
[*]Hopefully fixed the door getting stuck bug
[*]Fixed bug with blink cover not covering entire screen
[*]Fixed bug with SCP-939 playing lure sound when sleeping
[*]Fixed bug with SCPs not stopping a hunt when getting shocked
[*]Fixed bug with main menu wallpapers having incorrect aspect ratio
[/list]

Thanks for reading and have fun with SCP: Observer :D

notes.title: Version 1.5.0 - Foundation for Steam Workshop implementation
notes.content:
Greetings fellow researchers,

this is part 1 of this major effort to integrate the Steam Workshop into SCP: Observer. I have spent the last few weeks reworking some key systems to allow for an "easy" implementation of the Steam Workshop in the coming weeks.

Since many key systems have been changed, there may be some new bugs that I haven't found yet. If you find a bug I would be very grateful if you could report it.

More about the Steam Workshop implementation can be found after the changelist.

[h2]Full changelist[/h2]

The biggest changes were made in the background, where the player will not notice any difference. Nevertheless, there are still some new interesting changes.

[list]
[*] Revised the Custom Scenario menu ui
[*] Added a difficulty selection to the Custom Scenario
[*] Removed hard mode
[*] Revised some post processing effects
[*] Added a glitch effect to the security camera ui
[*] Other minor bugfixes and changes
[/list]

About the new difficulty selection. The difficulty level determines how much additional power will be consumed and how many server outages will occur during the scenario.

[h2]Steam Workshop[/h2]

Before I begin, I want to point out that most of this is still experimental and subject to change.

I assume that most of you know what Steam Workshop is. Basically, players can upload the content they create and other players can download and play it.

To start off, I am planning 2 things that the workshop will support. The first thing will allow players to create their own scenario and the second thing will allow players to upload their own models for the SCPs.

[h3]Create custom maps[/h3]

Creating your own scenario is handled by a "Scenario Creator" within the game itself. I haven't tried this yet, but the bottom line is that players can place rooms from both the heavy and light containment zones and create their own map that way. Players can also choose which SCP they want in the scenario and place nodes (waypoints) for them. These maps are initially saved locally and can be uploaded to the Steam Workshop if needed.

To make things even more interesting, I would also like to add variants of the security room with 1, 3 and 4 entrances.

Other players can then download these maps from the Steam Workshop and once downloaded they will appear in the custom scenario selection window (currently there are only the two official scenarios created by me).

[h3]SCP model change[/h3]

On the second point, there is not much to say yet, but I think it would be good to change the model for the SCPs.

Thanks for reading. I have no idea how long it will take, but if you are interested I will post regular updates on my [url=https://discord.gg/fYgStSzqST]Discord[/url].

notes.title: Version 1.4.0 - Localization Support + New Hardmode
notes.content:
Greetings survivors,

I have some important new announcements to make. 

First off all, SCP: Observer now supports German and French as languages you can choose. Other languages like Spanish, Portuguese and more will follow in future updates. 

Next, I overhauled and improved the user interface to make it more user-friendly, such as showing renderings of the SCP in the Custom Scenario selection screen. I've also removed the document database and replaced it with a more practical survival guide that can be accessed from the main menu. 

For new players who are still learning the game, I disabled some cameras that are basically useless in early scenarios. This helps new players focus on the important cameras.

Last but not least, the new hard mode. It is characterized by the merging of the SCPs from both zones and a slightly higher power consumption as well as server malfunctions.

[h2]Full changelist[/h2]

[list]
[*] Added localization for French and German
[*] Added a new Hardmode challenge
[*] Added a Survival Guide which replaces the Document Database
[*] Added SCP icons for Custom Scenario selection screen
[*] Disabled some cameras in early scenarios to help new players
[*] Removed SCP-303 easter egg (He will be implemented somewhere else)
[*] SCP-096 is now more active in Custom Scenarios
[*] Revised SCP-3199 document
[*] Many small bugfixes
[/list]

As for the French localization, I am not an expert in this language, the most I could say is my name. So if you notice a problem with the localization, please let me know on [url=https://discord.gg/fYgStSzqST]Discord[/url] or by creating a new discussion on Steam. The same goes for everything else in this game. I'm always happy to hear suggestions and even bug reports.

Thanks to all of you for all the positive reviews on Steam and for playing the game. I still have a long list of things that need to be done, like some kind of ending and I want to add more Easter Eggs and little events that can happen in the game. I also had the idea of adding little independent mini-games (similar to the plush trap mini-game in Five Nights at Freddy's 4), but that's just an idea. 

As always, thank you all for reading and I hope you enjoy the new update.

notes.title: SCP: Observer is now available!
notes.content:
[h1]The wait is finally over![/h1]

In a little over 2 years I developed SCP: Observer as my first ever project in game development and programming in general. Originally, the game was not planned to be an SCP game, instead I wanted to make a Five Nights at Freddy's fan game. 
In the end, I'm very happy with how the game turned out, and none of this would have been possible without the help of the many beta testers.

[h2]Future plans[/h2]

SCP: Observer is a mostly finished product and I don't have any big plans for future updates. There probably won't be any new zones or main SCPs, instead I want to focus on fixing possible bugs and implementing new small features like new events. The future of this game strongly depends on the player feedback and what the players want.

Personally, I will focus on new projects, some of which are even in the SCP universe.

There is nothing more to say other than enjoy the game.

notes.title: Second Public Beta in March
notes.content:
[h2]Sign up now![/h2]

You can now sign up for the second Public Beta on the store page of SCP: Observer. By signing up you will automatically have access to the beta during this time period. Just like before, I encourage every player to give me feedback and tell me their thoughts about the game. Specifically I would like to improve the Heavy Containment Zone a lot more.

[h3]Public Beta Q&A[/h3]

Let's start with a little public beta Q&A to answer some general questions.

[b]What is the goal of the public beta?[/b]

The main goal of the public beta is to fix potential bugs and improve the game, before fully releasing it.

[b]When can I play the public beta?[/b]

You can play the beta from March 24, 2023, 1pm CET, until March 27, 2023, 8am CET. During this time, you can download the SCP: Observer Public Beta from your Steam library just like you could with the first beta.

[b]How will the public beta differ from the original game?[/b]

There will be no differences in gameplay between the public beta and the original game. The only difference is that the original game has Steam Achievements, which is not the case with the public beta. In addition, the progress made is not carried over into the real game.

[b]How to report bugs?[/b]

The best way to give feedback or report bugs is to join the official [url=https://discord.gg/fYgStSzqST]Discord server[/url] and use the channels inside the SCP: Observer category. If you want to do it directly in Steam you can create a new discussion on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1738710/discussions/]Discussion Board[/url].

[b]What plans do you have for SCP: Observer after the beta?[/b]

SCP: Observer is almost finished, but I plan to polish it more and add fix more bugs. I am also aiming for getting the game verified on the Steamdeck.

[h2]Major changes[/h2]

Let's start with the new audio overhaul. In previous versions, including the beta, you could only hear the sound from your own security room. Sounds from far away could not be heard with this system, such as the security doors in SCP-914's security chamber. The new system is designed to change that by allowing you to hear the sound from the camera you are watching. This makes using the cameras much more fun and immersive.

notes.title: Development News 02/01/2023
notes.content:
[h1]Happy New Year[/h1]

Today the waiting is finally over. The beta for SCP: Observer will be released today at 3pm CET. As the first Development News post of the new year and the last post before the start of the beta, I would like to make some more announcements.

[h2]Announcements[/h2]

I have a lot of major changes I want to cover in this post. First of all, I have disabled Early Access for SCP: Observer. The reason for this is that I want to release a fully playable and largely bug-free game. After the official game is released I don't plan on adding any new main SCPs or zones, just quality of life changes, new events or other small things and I don't need Early Access for that. This has no downside for you as a player, since you will be getting a fully playable game at release.

The next big change I want to announce is that I have removed SCP-966 from the game. The reason for this is that SCP-966 was a particularly difficult SCP to balance in the game. In my opinion, his mechanics with the infrared vision cameras were not suitable and destroyed some important game mechanics. That doesn't mean I won't add him back in the future, but he won't be a main SCP.

While trying to balance the Heavy Containment Zone and removing SCP-966 I realized that the old map was really unbalanced and too big. Therefore, I have revised the entire map Heavy Containment. The image below shows the new map. The dark red color indicates the room you are watching.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/RNuZGqm.png[/img]

I also added a camera action to start a camera scan. The camera scan shows the position of all detected SCPs on the camera map, by letting the corresponding rooms blinking in the same dark red color. After activating the scan, the output might look like the following image.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/vyE3L0m.png[/img]

Last but not least, I added the icons for usage, blink and stamina bars, as well as the icons for interaction and crouching.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/UwXOKiC.png[/img]

[h3]Public Beta Q&A[/h3]

Let's start with a little public beta Q&A to answer some general questions.

[b]What is the goal of the public beta?[/b]

The main goal of the public beta is to fix potential bugs and improve the game, before fully releasing it.

[b]When can I play the public beta?[/b]

There will be no differences in gameplay between the public beta and the original game. The only difference is that the original game has Steam Achievements, which is not the case with the public beta.

[b]How to report bugs?[/b]

The best way to give feedback or report bugs is to create a new discussion on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1738710/discussions/]Discussion Board[/url]. You can also join the official [url=https://discord.gg/fYgStSzqST]Discord server[/url] where you can message me directly or use one of the channels dedicated to SCP: Observer.

[b]What plans do you have for SCP: Observer after the beta?[/b]

SCP: Observer is mostly finished, but I plan to add new events and improve current mechanics. Other things I'm aiming for are support for multiple operating systems, like the Steamdeck. This also means that there will probably be full controller support at some point in the future.

[h3]More announcements[/h3]

The system requirements for SCP: Observer are now available and can be viewed on the store page. Most of you will definitely be able to play it.

notes.title: Development News 09/11/2022
notes.content:
[h2]Apology to the SCP: Observer Community[/h2]

I apologize for the massive delay in development and news. I had a lot of problems in my personal life that I had to face, and during this time I was not able to invest the time in the development of this game that I would have otherwise liked to.

During the last 2 months I have redone SCP: Observer from scratch. This post will cover every major new addition or rework.

[h2]Major changes[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41163729/67a135d755218467aae86a98b6e7f67cd73dfaab.png[/img]

As you can see in the image above, I've reworked the camera interface and action system that I talked about in a previous post. To complement this, I added a new way to move through the cameras. By pressing W, A, S or D you can move to the next connected room in the corresponding direction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41163729/5edb9d57668d022e68e1a1e4e5105dfedeb4405b.png[/img]

The above map shows all rooms you can observe in the Light Containment Zone. The map below shows the same in the Heavy Containment Zone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41163729/32bb2d1d8709aab9014682afec23ac961b8566a9.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41163729/90a86c299bb89dbd75703043506ee618466b0aa1.png[/img]

The screenshot above shows the new SCP-035 model from SCP: Containment Breach. I'm not 100% satisfied with it, but in my opinion it's a huge improvement over the previous model.

[h2]Minor changes[/h2]

[list]
[*]Added new camera actions like closing doors
[*]New character controller similar to the one SCP: Containment Breach
[*]Security cameras rotate on their own
[*]Massive performance increase
[*]Reduced game size on disk by almost 500MB (Current total size: 529MB)
[/list]

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

I hope this post has given back some hope that this game will ever be released. For now, all I can say is that I have a release date planned for Q1 2023, as well as many new posts about the current status and progress. I am investing all my free time into this game to finish it in the given time frame. Thank you all for your understanding, here are some more screenshots.

notes.title: Development News 21/11/2021
notes.content:
[h2]What's new?[/h2]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/gA496Ai.png[/img]

I increased the overall brightness and the surveillance camera now looks more like a real CCTV camera. Glitch effects and slight distortions can be seen to emulate a surveillance camera.

Despite the fact that [b]SCP-3199[/b] is running towards you, you can also see a button with a camera icon in it. The button is used to switch between a different camera perspective. These buttons are present in some rooms to observe blind spots.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Tt2vxz5.png[/img]

Similar to the camera button, there is also a button that allows you to activate a [b]Tesla Gate[/b]. This can help you to survive or maybe it just makes them more angry.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/u8sxxhO.png[/img]

The picture above shows the perspective outside of a surveillance camera. The look of the GUI may change in the future.

At the edge of the image you can see a bunch of monitors. They can be used to observe some rooms without directly entering the camera system. They may save your live in some situations, but you still need to monitor the cameras manually if you want to survive.

The picture also shows the generator I talked about in the previous post.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WvvEloC.png[/img]

I removed a lot of unnecessary hallways from the Light Containment map. This makes it easier to follow the path of an SCP without getting confused.

You can move the camera map around using the WASD keys. Note that some rooms are not yet visible on this image, such as room SCP-173.

notes.title: Development News 26/9/2021
notes.content:
[h3]Major changes[/h3]

The Light Containment Zone is nearly finished and currently contains 3 main SCP entities, but there will be added more, before the game gets released.

The surveillance camera system is revised and now much more interesting. You can switch cameras in specific rooms to get a different perspective or reach blind spots. I'm also planning on adding more features to the camera system in the future.

An early version of a generator got added to the Security Room where you can regain small amounts of power as well as a ventilation system you should keep an eye on, who knows what can come through these vents.

There are also ideas about more interaction with the world around you and object SCPs you can use to defend yourself, an example would be SCP-268.
